missionPremise: A-205 (measured 2026-09-17, OPS-16 row P-305, and the canary proof _inbox/2026-09-17_p249_canary_proof.md): P-251 rotated HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY across five Cloud Run services end to end, but its SIXTH consumer — Vercel project `property-explorer` — carries its own synced copy of the same value as HAUSKA_RETRIEVAL_API_KEY / RETRIEVAL_API_KEY, and the workflow that writes that copy (hauska-map .github/workflows/property-explorer-sync-retrieval-key.yml) authoritative-replaces the PRODUCTION environment only. The Preview environment kept the pre-rotation value, so every Property Explorer preview answered its panel read with {"error":"retrieval_auth_failed","message":"Property atom chain retrieval returned HTTP 401 ..."} (a 401 upstream wrapped by the panel). Nothing noticed until a staging proof needed a preview. The discovery method could not have seen it: `gcloud run services describe` structurally cannot list a Vercel project, which is exactly why the sixth consumer was missed. vercel env pull returns sensitive values empty, so the two environments cannot be compared by value — the SURFACE is the measurable thing. The ruling this rests on is the operator's, A-205: card the stale Preview key and the class it belongs to.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate all three without me: (1) `node scripts/check-preview-key-drift.mjs --selftest` exits 0, and `--url <a live preview>` exits 0 on a preview whose credential leg answers and exits 3 on one whose panel read carries an auth marker, with exit 4 for anything not gradeable; (2) `90_runbooks/key_rotation_all_environments.md` exists, names Production, Preview and Development for every consumer it lists, names the instrument as the closing check, and states that no such runbook existed before it; (3) `node scripts/inventory-key-consumers.mjs` produces a listing that names every Vercel project holding one of the three names by environment and every Cloud Run resource doing the same, with every unreadable listing named and every reach-limit stated as a gap. Each of the three has a filed artifact and a run in this close's evidence list. The rows own reading of `status` is closed-partial, because the check has not yet run for real on a stale environment and the hauska-map half is an unmerged draft — both are stated below rather than narrated away.
scopeBasis: The three deliverables are exactly the dispatch's 'What to build' items 1-3, at the dispatch's own paths. Included beyond a literal reading, each with its reason: (a) the hauska-map draft PR, which the dispatch permits 'if a code check belongs there' — it is the PREVENTIVE half, because the same workflow that missed Preview will miss it again by construction on the next rotation, and the runbook names it as an open hole until merged and run; (b) a live negative control, because every pre-registered live run was expected to PASS and an indicator never observed firing is not observed; (c) the alias set in the inventory, reported separately from the predicate, because A-205 itself ran through an alias.
